commitments.text: NCL must return all disturbed lands to their original condition or as agreed upon with authorities having jurisdiction in respect to said lands, if NCL begins construction of any component of the Project but does not complete construction and obtain 'Leave to Open' for the gas processing facility.
NCL must notify the Executive Director of any plans to abandon the Project prior to operation.

The construction, operation, and eventual reclamation and site restoration of the proposed West Stoddart Gas Processing Facility will generate a variety of wastes. These will be managed according to a waste management plan stressing waste minimization, reuse, recycling, recovery, and, when required, treatment and disposal, consistent with the B.C. Industrial Pollution Prevention Program, Waste Management Act, Oil and Gas Production Waste Control Regulation, and Environmental Operating Guidelines for the British Columbia Upstream Petroleum Industry.

NCL will prepare an emergency response and implementation plan to ensure that West Stoddart Gas Project employees and contractors respond effectively to emergency situations. Specific project features to be addressed include the potential for uncontrolled sour gas release from the plant site, gathering pipeline or acid gas injection system, and the potential for Liquids, condensate, and produced water spills during trucking operations. Emergency response plans will be developed in consultation with area residents, local and regional government agencies and provincial regulatory agencies according to CAN/CSA-Z731-95 Emergency Planning for Industry.

In order to ensure an effective response in the event of an emergency at the West Stoddart Gas facility, NCL will develop and maintain an effective training program with project operations personnel and contractors which will include conducting regular mock emergency training exercises.

In order to ensure that proper measures are in place to respond to a pipeline or trucking related spill, NCL will prepare an Environmental Procedures Manual. The objective of the manual will be to ensure that personnel are familiar with environmental regulations, waste management, spill response and containment and reporting requirements.

At the end of the useful life of the facility, facilities will be dismantled and the site remediated and reclaimed to a condition suitable for forest regeneration. Prior to construction, the top soil and organic layer will be salvaged and stored to facilitate eventual reclamation of the site, and the storage area will be marked on the plant plot plans.

Predisturbance drainage patterns will be re-established after construction. Silt traps and diversion berms will be placed at regular intervals along rights-of-way in order to minimize soil erosion until appropriate vegetation can re-establish; where necessary the upper slopes of these berms will be reinforced with slash or sandbags. Diversion ditches or berms will be installed at the base of all slopes adjacent to wetlands. Slope stability and erosion will be monitored and managed throughout the operational period of the pipelines.

The locations of the two access roads were selected to follow existing cutlines in order to minimize new land disturbance in the area. Due to the route selection process undertaken, there will be approximately 1 hectare of additional land disturbance due to the upgrading of the access roads for the West Stoddart project.

NCL has made a commitment to First Nations, other groups and individuals to continue to provide ongoing communications regarding the West Stoddart Project through correspondence, information updates, telephone calls, personal contacts and formal and informal meetings. NCL has established a toll free Community Affairs line, will hold Employment and Contract Opportunity Workshops, and will place copies of the application in the Fort St. John public library and the Taylor Town Office for public review.

There is a high concentration of sites recorded in the immediate vicinity of the Stoddart (Fish) Creek crossing. Deeply buried archaeological resources could be present at this creek crossing. Monitoring of the ditching operation is deemed warranted during construction.

Among the mitigation measures being undertaken by Novagas to reduce air emissions is the adoption of acid gas injection to reduce the potential for chronic acid forming emissions from SO2. NOx emissions will be reduced per unit of product produced by utilizing energy efficient equipment at the West Stoddart Plant.

NCL recognizes and respects the treaty rights of the First Nations within the proposed project area. Blueberry River Band concerns (a liaison person, sensitivities around the Charlie Lake area including a burial site, and potential residential gas supply to the Blueberry Reserve) were mitigated by an ongoing commitment to consultation, including retaining a liaison person and open houses, a traditional overview walk, and environmental monitors retained during construction.

In the unlikely possibility that archaeological resources are uncovered during the construction phase of the project, it is recommended that all ground altering activity in the area of the find(s) cease and the Archaeology Branch in Victoria be contacted for further instructions. If required Heritage North will be available for inspecting and assessing the significance of the find(s).

In a non-archaeological context, Novagas should note the locations of the historic and traditional use sites. Novagas may wish to contact the Fort St. John-North Peace Museum regarding the historic site location at HbRe-t36, and may wish to discuss protective measures at the two traditional use locations with the Chiefs and Councils of Blueberry and Doig First Nations.
